newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge rejects Democratic Party finance suit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge rejects Democratic Party finance suit.

text.p: A judge Friday rejected a Republican Party request for an injunction to force the Democratic Party to file a final, pre-election financial report with the Federal Election Commission (FEC).

U.S. District Judge Paul Friedman dismissed the lawsuit, ruling from the bench that the court lacks jurisdiction because the complaint first must be taken up by FEC, an agency responsible for election financing laws.
A lawyer for the Democratic National Committee (DNC) told the judge during the two-hour hearing the report finally was filed on Friday morning.
The report at issue covers information about contributions and spending in the first two weeks of October. It had been due last week.
The Democratic Party initially said it did not have to file the report because it did not spend any money directly on behalf of President Bill Clinton or other candidates during the period.

But after a political uproar following disclosure of this decision on Tuesday, party officials immediately moved to file 500 pages of fundraising data and promised the final report by the end of this week.
A DNC spokeswoman told reporters the only addition in the report from the earlier data was a $500,000 contribution from Arnold Hiatt of STRIDE RITE Corp.

The judge noted the report had been filed, but expressed reluctance to declare the controversy moot or judicially irrelevant because the Republican Party did not immediately know if it contained all the required information.

"The fact of the matter is even if the DNC is in violation of the law or regulation, this court doesn't have jurisdiction to deal with the complaint at this stage, absent the exhaustion of administrative remedies," he said.

The judge based his decision on a ruling last month by a U.S. appeals court rejecting Texas billionaire Ross Perot's lawsuit seeking to be included in the presidential debates. The ruling said he first must go to the federal elections agency.

The Republican Party had wanted the court to require that the report be filed immediately, but did not pursue an earlier demand seeking to stop Democratic Party spending until it was submitted. It also has filed a complaint with the FEC.
The judge said the complaint must proceed first before the FEC, a requirement set by Congress in drafting the law and a process that he admitted could take months.
David Norcross, Republican National Committee general counsel, said afterwards that a decision would be made soon on whether to go to the U.S. Court of Appeals.
Lawyers for both sides engaged in angry partisan wrangling during the hearing.
"This is a case that should never have been filed," Democratic Party lawyer Paul Smith charged. "It is basically a publicity stunt."
Republican Party lawyer George Terwilliger shot back, "The DNC has a duty to obey the law, just like anybody else." He added, "We think it is a serious matter."
